compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX 5090M Blackwell, 82 SMs, 32KB groupshared cap in DXIL path. Tensor cores not directly usable from HLSL cs_6_8 here.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Most ops are tiny GEMMs (32x32, 32x96, 32x128) per window of 16 tokens; compute is modest. Main work is the 2 LN, attention (16x16 tokens), MLP (32->128->32). With B*nH*nW=180*320=57600 windows of N=16 tokens each, total tokens=921600.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Naive per-token threading underutilizes; per-window threadgroup likely optimal.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input is 29.49M fp16 elements = ~59MB; fits in 64MB L2 partially. Output 59MB. Weights are tiny (<20KB) and reusable across all windows -> cache-resident easily. Bottleneck is global load/store of activations once each if fused.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Multiple global round-trips between sub-stages would dominate; full fusion needed.

register_pressure.notes: Per window (16 tokens x 32 ch fp16) = 512 fp16 = 1KB. Per thread if 1 token/thread: 32 fp16 = small. Hidden MLP 128: 128 fp16 per token = 256B/thread, fine.
register_pressure.risk: Low pressure; comfortable register residency for per-window working set.

nodes.notes:
1) CLASSIFICATION: Fused Swin transformer block (no shift, single-head, window=4x4). Mixed: LayerNorm + linear projections + small attention (softmax+matmul) + MLP (GELU). Dense access. Window N=16 tokens, C=32, hidden=128. Input (1,720,1280,32) tiled into nH=180, nW=320 -> 57600 independent windows.
2) MATH: Per window of 16 tokens c32: ln1 -> qkv(32->96) -> attn 16x16 + rpe + softmax -> *V -> proj(32->32) + residual1 -> ln2 -> fc1(32->128) -> GELU -> fc2(128->32) + residual2. All reductions are within a 16-token window or within C=32/hidden=128.
3) LAYOUT: x is (B,H,W,C) row-major contiguous; window partition is a permute. Window index (wh,ww) maps to H tile rows of 4 and W tile cols of 4. Per-window 16 tokens reside in non-contiguous H rows but contiguous within each row of 4. Weights tiny: qkv 3072 fp16=6KB; proj 1KB; fc1 4096=8KB; fc2 4096=8KB; norms+biases trivial; rpe 256=0.5KB. Total weights ~25KB, fits in L2 trivially, fits in groupshared if needed.
4) REGIMES: (a) bandwidth-bound: streaming input once + output once dominates -> aim for single fused kernel, ~118MB traffic at 896GB/s ~0.13ms floor. (b) latency-bound for tiny windows if 1 threadgroup per window with under-utilization. (c) compute-bound on MLP fc1/fc2: 16*32*128*2 + 16*128*32*2 = 262K flops/window * 57600 ~15GF, trivial. So memory-bound is dominant.
5) KNOBS: threadgroup size (e.g., 32 threads = 1 warp per window, or 64 = 2 warps for 2 windows); per-window mapping (1 thread per token vs cooperative); weight residency (registers via constants vs groupshared vs reload from L2); softmax via wave intrinsics; GELU approximation; vectorized float16_t4 loads.
6) SKELETON: Each threadgroup processes K windows. Load 16 tokens*32ch into registers/groupshared. Apply LN1 (reduce over C=32 within wave). Compute QKV by mat-vec into registers. Compute attn = q@k^T (16x16), add rpe, softmax (reduce over 16). Compute attn@v -> token. proj + residual. LN2 over C=32. fc1 mat-vec into 128 hidden registers. GELU. fc2 mat-vec back to 32. Add residual2. Store. Weights stay in L2 (cache) or load to groupshared once per group.
7) FAMILIES:
 - F1 Per-window threadgroup (32 threads, 1 warp): each thread = 1 of 16 tokens (16 active) or 2 tokens, uses wave intrinsics for LN/softmax/matmul reductions. Strength: minimal sync, fully register-resident. Limiter: thread underutilization at N=16.
 - F2 Multi-window per threadgroup: pack 4-8 windows into a 128-256 thread group sharing weight loads in groupshared. Strength: amortize weight load, higher occupancy. Weakness: more groupshared, sync needs.
 - F3 Per-token thread (3-pass kernels): split-stage; rejected because it forces global round-trips, dominating BW. Full fusion preferred.
Full-fusion is register-feasible (per-token state ~32-128 fp16 fits easily in 255 regs), so single fused kernel is the top choice.

action.description: Build the initial fully-fused single-pass HLSL kernel: one threadgroup of 32 threads (single warp) processes one 4x4 window. Each thread handles one of 16 tokens (16 active lanes, optionally 2 tokens/thread to use all 32). Sequence: load token (32 fp16) from global into registers; layernorm via wave reductions; QKV matvec with weights streamed from L2; compute attn=q.k^T cross-token via wave shuffles + rpe load + softmax via wave max/sum; attn@v via wave shuffles; proj + residual1 in registers; ln2; fc1 to 128 hidden in registers; GELU; fc2 to 32; add residual2; write back. No groupshared except possibly tiny rpe/weights staging.
action.rationale: Establishes the maximally fused baseline that eliminates intermediate global traffic. With ~118MB input+output, theoretical floor ~0.13ms. Tiny weights stay L2-resident across all 57600 windows.
action.title: F1: Single-warp-per-window fully fused kernel

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does=Single warp (32 threads, 16 active) per 4x4 window does LN1->QKV->attn(softmax)->proj+res->LN2->FC1+GELU+FC2+res fully in registers, using WaveReadLaneAt for K/V exchange. bottleneck=compute+register pressure: each active lane does ~6k MACs scalar fp32 with HIDDEN=128 reg array (h[128]) creating spill risk; half the warp idle (16/32 lanes). PERF_GAP: expected 3.0x vs observed 1.21x — gap explained by (a) only 16 active lanes wasting warp issue, (b) scalar fp32 MAC throughput not using tensor cores or fp16 packing, (c) huge unrolled loops causing register spills/long shader. FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: F1 fused design works and passes, but yields modest speedup; next bet is to (i) use all 32 lanes (2 tokens/thread or two windows/warp) and (ii) replace scalar fp32 matmuls with fp16 dot4/dot2 packed math or wave-collaborative GEMM.

action.description: Pack 4 windows (64 tokens) per threadgroup with 128 threads (4 warps), sharing one staged copy of weights (qkv/proj/fc1/fc2) and rpe in groupshared (~25KB, under 32KB cap). Each warp handles one window using the same wave-intrinsic recipe as F1. Goal: amortize weight loads and improve SM occupancy/issue rate.
action.rationale: If L2 weight reuse already saturates, groupshared staging may not help; but it can reduce L1/L2 pressure and increase warps-per-SM. Worth comparing vs F1.
action.title: F2: Multi-warp threadgroup with groupshared staging

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: 25KB groupshared near the 32KB DXIL cap. Need to confirm occupancy with that allocation.

action.description: Optimize the global memory access by coalescing the window-partition gather: for each window's 4 rows of 4 contiguous tokens (4*32 fp16 = 256B per row), use vectorized float16_t4 loads and ensure threads within a wave read contiguous addresses. Likewise for the output write. Combine with F1 mapping (token-to-thread arranged so consecutive lanes hit consecutive global addresses within each of the 4 rows of the window).
action.rationale: Window-partition is the only non-trivial access pattern. Coalescing the 4 rows separately (each row is contiguous 16 fp16 channels x 4 tokens) hits peak BW.
action.title: Coalesced vectorized input gather/output scatter

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does: 2 windows packed per warp (half-warp per window, 16 lanes per window owning 1 token each); fully fused LN1->QKV->Attn(via WaveReadLaneAt)->Proj->LN2->FC1+GELU->FC2 with per-thread registers for x_in/xn/q/k/v/ao/r1/xn2 and h[128]. bottleneck: compute + register pressure from h[128] FC1 intermediate and per-thread C=32 inner products; some bandwidth on weight reloads since weights are not shared across lanes.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes (packed 2 windows/warp realized as sub=t>>4).
UPDATE_BELIEF: 1.85x measured matches the 1.8x prediction closely; lane utilization fix paid off. Next bet: attack h[128] register footprint and FC1/FC2 compute via wave-cooperative MLP (lanes share weights and partition the 128 hidden units), or use float16_t4 vectorized weight loads to reduce L1/L2 pressure.

action.title: fp16/dot4 packed matmuls + reduce register pressure

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: distinct from n1a because it tackles arithmetic precision/throughput and register spill of h[128], not lane utilization. Use half precision accumulation where safe, dot()/mad with float16_t4 vector loads on weights, and stream FC1->FC2 to avoid materializing h[128] fully (e.g., tile HIDDEN in chunks of 32 to keep <=32 regs live). Reduces spills and boosts FP throughput.

action.title: Wave-cooperative FC1/FC2: partition HIDDEN=128 across 16 lanes/window (8 each), eliminate h[128] register array

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does=Single warp processes 2 windows; each lane owns 1 token; FC1 produces 8 hidden units/lane, fc2 reduced via WaveReadLaneAt across 16 lanes. bottleneck=correctness (failed eval, max_diff=3.64). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: Correctness failed — likely cause: lane indexing for fc1 outputs. Code uses hidden_idx=token_id*8+kk, but fc2 expects fc2w[oc*HIDDEN+hi] with hi matching producer lane's hidden index. The reduction sums part[oc] across lanes l in [0,16), so each lane l must own hidden units [l*8..l*8+8); however token_id (per-window lane index) is correct. The bug is more likely: h_local indexing vs fc2w layout mismatch, OR the residual add 'r1[oc] + s' is correct only if s includes fc2b once — currently fc2b is added once which is fine. Most probable: fc1w/fc2w layout assumption — fc1w may be [HIDDEN][C] or [C][HIDDEN]; verify. next bet: Debug fc1w/fc2w layout (transpose) before claiming approach broken. PERF_GAP: expected 2.4x, observed FAIL.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: distinct LDS-based approach; only one barrier after cooperative load. Mutually exclusive with n1a1 (which removes the need by partitioning) and n1a2 (which keeps SRV loads). Risk: extra barrier and limited reuse if only 2 windows/group; may need larger groups (e.g., 4-8 windows) to amortize.

action.title: Fix wave-cooperative FC1/FC2 correctness: verify fc1w/fc2w layout and lane->hidden mapping

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: child (debug-and-improve) of n1a1, not a sibling alternative. Re-examine indexing: fc1w[o*32+c] with o=token_id*8+kk maps lane l to hidden indices [l*8, l*8+8). fc2w[oc*HIDDEN+hi] must use the same hi. If reference uses fc1w stored as [HIDDEN,C] row-major, indexing is fine. Suspect bug: WaveReadLaneAt loop across 16 lanes only reads lanes [lane_base..lane_base+15], but if warp packs 2 windows (sub=0/1), lane_base correctly selects half. Possible real bug: in attention K/V wave shuffle path interaction with later FC reductions (uniform control flow?). Try: (a) keep h[128] register array but compute FC2 cooperatively only, (b) ensure WaveReadLaneAt is called from uniform control flow with [unroll]. Plan: revert to per-lane full HIDDEN=128 with 8-wide vectorized loop (no cross-lane reduction) and measure; if correct, reintroduce cooperation step-by-step.

kernel_summary: Fused simplified Swin transformer block over a (1,720,1280,32) fp16 feature map with window=4x4 (N=16 tokens), single head, no shift: LayerNorm -> QKV(32->96) -> scaled dot-product attention with RPE -> proj(32->32) + residual -> LayerNorm -> fc1(32->128) -> GELU -> fc2(128->32) + residual. 57600 independent windows; tiny weights (~25KB total) easily L2-resident; per-window working set fits in registers (16 tokens x 32 ch). Memory-bound (~118MB activation traffic; floor ~0.13ms at 896GB/s). Best strategy: full fusion in a single compute shader, one warp per window with wave intrinsics for LN/softmax/attention reductions, coalesced fp16 vector loads/stores. Constraints: cs_6_8, 32KB groupshared cap, prefer register residency, minimize barriers.
open_questions: Does Buffer<float16_t> support vectorized loads, or must we use ByteAddressBuffer + Load2/Load4 to coalesce fp16x4 reads?
What is the optimal threadgroup size: 32 threads (1 warp = 1 window with 2 tokens/thread) vs 64/128 (multiple windows sharing groupshared weights)?
Is L2 sufficient to keep all ~25KB weights resident across 57600 windows, or do we need explicit groupshared staging to avoid repeated L2 fetches?
Should LayerNorm accumulate mean/variance in fp32 (matching PyTorch reference) to meet rtol/atol=0.01, and is fp16 accumulation in the small GEMMs accurate enough?
Which GELU approximation (tanh-based vs erf-based) matches the PyTorch fp16 reference within tolerance?
How are the 16 tokens of a window laid out in memory after window_partition, and what is the most coalesced gather pattern (per row of 4 contiguous tokens)?
Does the dispatch need exact integer group counts equal to nH*nW=57600 (e.g., dispatch [320,180,1]), and does the launch.json shape align with that?
Are wave intrinsics (WaveActiveSum/Max, WaveReadLaneAt) reliably available and performant on RTX 5090 Mobile under cs_6_8?
